reroute_reason: Bundle was well routed: five retrievals, all evidence_only, covering both sides of the alleged conflict (T2S baseline schedule and RTS cut-off structure for R2026.JUN; Porto Notice 394/2024 timetable; Porto published CET operating-hours table with the WET note; Porto Operational Manual Chapter 12/§12.1). The one genuinely missing item, Operational Manual Chapter 4 'Schedule and Timetables', has no route in topic-index.json (Porto routes checked: no schedule/timetable question_type beyond porto_operating_hours_published and timetable_document_scope, both already in the bundle), so no corrected context existed to request. It is reported as an Open item instead.
notes: Answer resolves the apparent conflict as a clock-convention difference rather than a substantive one: Notice 394/2024 prints 17h00m on the Portuguese local clock, the Porto operating-hours page and the T2S UDFS R2026.JUN print 18:00 CET for the FOP cut-off, and the page states Portugal uses WET (-1 hour than CET). Support is an eleven-pair value-by-value alignment between the Notice and the CET/UDFS values (17h45m/18:45, 19h00m/20:00, 17h00m/18:00, 15h00m/16:00, all five partial windows, both maintenance windows), labelled Reasoned inference because the Notice does not state its own clock and its LIMITATION says conversion is not certified. Two premise corrections are made: (1) the retrieved Operational Manual excerpt contains no cut-off times at all and defers to Chapter 4, so the 17:00 figure in reviewed evidence comes from Notice 394/2024, not the Manual; (2) the Notice labels 17h00m 'Closing (end of day)', not 'FOP cut-off'. Qualifications kept attached: Portuguese governing text for both Porto sources (Notice English translation expressly not legally binding; Manual V43 operative effective date unresolved), UDFS body language English with no authoritative language and no independent whole-edition approval certification, R2026.JUN release identity, CET source convention with no UTC conversion, nominal-not-guaranteed and no-local-participant-cut-off limitation, and the need for a dated event overlay for any actual business date. All five retrievals were evidence_only and this is disclosed explicitly. Checker: 9/9 passed on the first run; no fix round was needed.
